init.welcomeDesc: Git identities and encrypted private keys stay on this device. Choose how to start:
init.createDesc: First-time setup. Create a local access password and recovery key.
init.createDescMobile: Brand new setup. Create an encrypted database, access password, and offline recovery key.
init.restoreDesc: You already have another device. Enter cloud storage and that device’s recovery key.
init.restoreDescMobile: The computer must already be synced to the cloud. Scan the QR to write cloud settings, then enter the recovery key.
init.restoreDescMobilePick: Already have data on a computer? Scan the QR to import cloud settings, then enter the old recovery key.
init.chooseDesc: Create a workspace if this is a new setup. Restore from the cloud with the other device’s recovery key if you already have data.

titles.oldRecovery: Enter the old device recovery key

descs.create0: Keys and config files are encrypted in your local folder and never uploaded in plaintext.
descs.create1: This password unlocks the app on this device. If you forget it, only the recovery key can reset access.
descs.create2: The recovery key is shown once. It is the only way to recover a new machine or a forgotten password. Store it offline.
descs.create3: Paste the recovery key you just saved to confirm you actually wrote it down.
descs.create4: The encrypted workspace is ready. You can start using the app.
descs.restore0: Restored identities and keys will be written into this local folder. Choose an empty folder that is not initialized.
descs.restore1: Enter the exact same R2 / S3 connection details (including prefix) as the old device.
descs.restore2: Enter the recovery key saved when the old device was initialized, to decrypt cloud data.
descs.restore3: Set a daily access password for this device. It can differ from the old one. The old recovery key stays valid.
descs.restore4: The workspace was rebuilt with the same master key. Both devices can keep syncing.

init.needPath: Choose or enter a workspace folder
init.scanQrTitle: Scan the cloud config QR on the computer
init.alreadyCreated: A workspace was already created at “{{path}}”. Changing the folder creates a new one; the old folder is not deleted.
init.pickEmpty: Choose an empty folder that has not been initialized yet.
init.wsDirPh: Click Browse, or paste a path
init.pathHint: Use a local standalone folder with ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens, e.g. D:\git-keymaster-ws. Avoid OneDrive / Nutstore, spaces, or non-ASCII paths (Git / OpenSSH often break).
init.createdKeepKey: The workspace already exists. Changing the password here only updates the access password; the recovery key stays the same.
init.newDirWarn: A new workspace (and a new recovery key) will be created in the new folder.
init.passwordLocal: The access password is only used locally for encryption checks. Remember it.
init.recoveryOnce: This is the only time the full recovery key is shown. Copy it and store it offline now.
init.pasteRecovery: Paste the recovery key you just saved:
init.recoveryPh: Paste or type the recovery key (e.g. GAM1-...)
init.readyDesc: You can import existing SSH keys or create Git identities for multiple hosts.
init.restoreCloudHint: These details must match the old device exactly. Need help? Open the guided setup to create a bucket and keys.
init.restoreCloudHintMobile: The computer must already have pushed to the cloud. Scanning only imports storage settings, not the recovery key.
init.restoreKeyWarn: Enter the recovery key saved on the old device (GAM1-…). The wrong key cannot decrypt cloud data.
init.restoreKeyWarnMobile: Scanning only wrote cloud settings. Enter the old device recovery key to unlock the vault. The QR does not contain it.
init.previewRepos: · plus {{count}} repo records from other machines
init.willRestore: About to restore {{identities}} identities and {{keys}} keys to “{{path}}”.
init.willImportRepos: Also import {{count}} repo records (paths remapped for this machine).
init.noImportRepos: Repo records from other machines will not be imported.
init.localPwHint: You can set a new local access password. Keep the old recovery key safe.
init.restoredFallback: The workspace was rebuilt with the same master key.
init.strength: Password strength: {{level}} (at least 8 characters; letters, digits, or symbols help)
init.scopeCoreHint: Global identities, encrypted private keys, and the local SSH bridge bootstrap.
init.scopeReposHint: Folder paths from other machines usually do not exist here. Leave this off for a clean local list; you can scan and import later.
init.mobileQrTitle: Scan the config QR on the computer
init.mobileQrDesc: On the computer open Settings → Cloud sync → Share config, then scan the QR to import connection details.

settings.title: Settings
settings.desc: Workspace security, app preferences, and account settings

language.title: Interface language
language.hint: Changes apply immediately — no restart. Start menu / Dock names follow the installer language and will not change here. A few backend errors may still be in Chinese in this release.

settings.appCardDesc: End-to-end encrypted vault and credential hub
settings.unlockAnimHint: Play a visual transition after a successful password unlock
settings.unlockAnimTip: Plays after you unlock with a password or recovery key. Silent grace unlocks do not trigger it.
settings.unlockAnimHintDesktop: When off, unlock goes straight to the main screen. Click or press Esc / Space / Enter to skip.
settings.launchTip: Open this app after you sign in. Windows uses the current-user Startup item; macOS uses Login Items. If grace unlock is on, keys may be loaded into ssh-agent.
settings.launchUnsupported: Launch at login is not supported on this system.
settings.launchHint: Example: turn this on after reinstalling on a travel laptop. Off by default.
settings.closeActionTip: What happens when you click the window close button.
settings.closeCurrent: Current: {{action}}. You can check “Remember my choice” in the confirmation. Reopening from the tray follows the grace-day setting.
settings.pwMin: New password must be at least 8 characters
settings.pwMismatch: The two new passwords do not match
settings.graceRange: Grace days must be between 0 and 30
settings.graceOff: Grace unlock disabled. The next launch needs the access password.
settings.graceOn: Grace unlock set for {{days}} day(s) after sign-in
settings.closeReset: Close action reset to ask every time

update.latest: You are on the latest version, or no update manifest was published yet.
update.manualOnly: This install cannot update in-app (for example a non-AppImage Linux package). Download manually.
update.skipped: Skipped {{version}}. Startup will not prompt again.
update.sourceDefault: Restored the default GitHub update source
update.autoTip: Silent check about 5 seconds after unlock. A toast appears if a new, unskipped version is found.
update.autoHint: You can still check manually when this is off.
update.sourceTip: Default is the built-in GitHub repo. You can switch to another repo or a static HTTPS manifest (internal mirror / other Git hosts). Installers must still pass the built-in public key check.
update.repoHint: Leave empty to use the factory default {{repo}}
update.prereleaseTip: Uses the GitHub Releases API and may include pre-releases.
update.toastManual: , download it manually for this install.
update.iosStoreOnly: On iOS, update from the App Store. In-app sideload is not available.
update.iosStoreSoon: The App Store link will be added after the listing is live.
update.sideloadHint: Downloads the release APK and opens the system installer. Allow unknown sources; the signing certificate must match this install.
update.installerOpened: The system installer is open. Confirm to replace this app.

proxy.title: Network proxy
proxy.enableTip: Applies only to requests from this app (updates, GitHub API, Git HTTPS, SSH, cloud sync). Does not change the system proxy.
proxy.hint: Turn on if GitHub / GitLab is unstable in your region. The password is stored in the local config file.
proxy.gitHttpsTip: Writes HTTP(S)_PROXY when this app runs git clone over HTTPS.
proxy.sshTip: Injects ProxyCommand for ssh / git launched by this app. Needs Git’s connect or ncat. Does not edit ~/.ssh/config.
proxy.cloudTip: R2 / S3 backups follow the master switch. Turn this off for domestic object storage.
proxy.httpsFail: GitHub HTTPS failed. Check the proxy.

security.intro1: This list only reads local config and the workspace path. Everything is computed on this device. No telemetry.
security.intro2: The OS will not tell this app who is watching the clipboard or capturing the screen, so we cannot name a listener.
security.intro3: Clipboard exclusion is a cooperative hint for history, cloud clipboards, and well-behaved managers. Malware can ignore it. It does not stop trojans or black out screenshots.
security.noTodos: Nothing pending. Passed checks are collapsed below.

factory.warn: This clears workspace data, restores the ~/.ssh entry, undoes user env / Git / terminal hooks written by this app, and deletes local config. Cloud data is not deleted. This cannot be undone.
factory.reconfirm: Type 清空 below, then run the reset. The confirmation word is always 清空.

pat.hint: Used to add public keys to GitHub and import org lists. Create a classic token with write:public_key or admin:public_key. The token is stored in the vault and never shown again here.
pat.tokenTip: Create it in GitHub Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens. It is verified immediately after save.

pages.overviewDesc: Keys, SSH config, agent, and connectivity for every Git identity
pages.totpDesc: Codes stay masked until you reveal them. Switch between cards and a list.
pages.accountsDesc: Group multiple logins per site. Passwords and linked 2FA stay masked.
pages.syncDesc: Pulls once at startup, then follows the schedule and local edits. Opening this page does not probe the cloud again.
pages.noIdentities: No Git identities yet. Create them on a computer, then sync to this phone.
